topic: CompTIA Security+ (SY0-701) exam preparation - the industry-standard entry-level cybersecurity certification covering security concepts, threats and mitigations, security architecture, security operations, and security program management
exam_format: Maximum 90 questions, 90 minutes, passing score 750 on a scale of 100-900. Question types include multiple choice, multiple response, and performance-based questions (PBQs - interactive simulations that appear first). Delivered online-proctored or at a Pearson VUE test center. SY0-701 is the CURRENT version (launched November 2023). The certification is valid for 3 years and renewable via continuing education (CE).
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple response clearly marked as 'Select TWO/THREE'
audience: Aspiring cybersecurity analysts, IT support and network professionals moving into security, help-desk and sysadmin staff, and career changers entering cyber. Recommended background is CompTIA Network+ and ~2 years of IT administration with a security focus, though many start here. A natural feeder to the CompTIA SecAI+ (AI security) course in this catalog.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: General Security Concepts
domains.notes: Foundational vocabulary and principles the rest of the exam builds on. Security controls: categories (technical, managerial, operational, physical) and types (preventive, deterrent, detective, corrective, compensating, directive). Fundamental concepts: CIA triad, non-repudiation, AAA (authentication, authorization, accounting) for people and systems, gap analysis, zero trust (control plane vs data plane, policy engine/administrator/enforcement point), physical security, deception and disruption technology (honeypots, honeynets, honeytokens). Change management and its security impact: approval, ownership, backout plans, maintenance windows, documentation. Cryptographic solutions: PKI (public/private keys, key escrow), symmetric vs asymmetric, hashing, digital signatures, certificates and CAs, key exchange, encryption levels (full-disk, file, database, transport), TPM/HSM/secure enclave, blockchain, obfuscation (steganography, tokenization, data masking), salting, key stretching.

domains.name: Threats, Vulnerabilities, and Mitigations
domains.notes: Threat actors and motivations: nation-state, unskilled attacker, hacktivist, insider threat, organized crime, shadow IT; attributes and motivations (data exfiltration, espionage, financial, disruption). Threat vectors and attack surfaces: message-based (email, SMS), image/file/voice, removable media, vulnerable software, unsupported systems, supply chain, social engineering (phishing, pretexting, BEC, watering hole). Vulnerability types: application (memory injection, buffer overflow, race conditions, malicious update), OS, web (SQLi, XSS), hardware (firmware, EoL, legacy), virtualization, cloud, supply-chain, cryptographic, misconfiguration, mobile, zero-day. Malicious activity indicators: malware (ransomware, trojan, worm, rootkit, keylogger), network/application/cryptographic attacks, password attacks. Mitigation techniques: segmentation, access control, isolation, patching, encryption, hardening, monitoring, least privilege, configuration enforcement.

domains.name: Security Architecture
domains.notes: Architecture models and their security implications: cloud (responsibility matrix, hybrid, third-party risks), IaC, serverless, microservices, network infrastructure (physical/software-defined), on-prem vs centralized vs decentralized, containerization, virtualization, IoT/ICS/SCADA/embedded, high availability. Secure enterprise infrastructure: device placement and attributes, security zones, attack surface, connectivity, failure modes (fail-open/closed), active vs passive controls, firewalls/IDS-IPS/proxies/load balancers, port security, VPN/TLS/IPSec/SD-WAN/SASE, selecting controls. Data protection: classification, types (regulated, PII, PHI, intellectual property), states (at rest, in transit, in use), sovereignty, methods (encryption, masking, tokenization, obfuscation, segmentation, permissions). Resilience and recovery: high availability, load balancing vs clustering, backups, continuity, testing (tabletop, failover, simulation), power (UPS/generators).

domains.name: Security Operations
domains.notes: The heaviest domain. Apply security to resources: secure baselines, hardening (mobile, workstations, servers, network devices, IoT, embedded), wireless/mobile (BYOD/COPE, MDM), WPA3/AAA/RADIUS. Asset management: acquisition, assignment, monitoring, inventory, disposal/sanitization. Vulnerability management: identification (scanning, threat intel, pen testing, bug bounty, CVE/CVSS), analysis, response (patching, remediation, exceptions), validation. Security monitoring and alerting: SIEM, log aggregation, SNMP, NetFlow, monitoring tools, alerting, scanning. Enterprise capabilities: firewalls, IDS/IPS, web/DNS filtering, email security (DKIM/DMARC/SPF), EDR/XDR, DLP, network access control. Identity and access management: provisioning, SSO (SAML, OAuth, OIDC), LDAP, federation, privileged access management, MFA factors, password concepts. Automation and orchestration (playbooks, SOAR). Incident response: process (preparation through lessons learned), training, testing, root cause, threat hunting, digital forensics. Data sources for investigation (logs, packet captures).

domains.name: Security Program Management and Oversight
domains.notes: Governance: policies (AUP, SDLC, disaster recovery), standards, procedures (onboarding/offboarding, change), guidelines, governance structures (boards, committees), roles (owner, controller, processor, custodian). Risk management: identification, assessment (ad hoc, recurring, one-time), analysis (qualitative/quantitative, SLE/ALE/ARO), risk register, appetite/tolerance, strategies (transfer, accept, avoid, mitigate), business impact analysis (RTO, RPO, MTTR, MTBF). Third-party/vendor risk: assessment, penetration testing, agreements (SLA, MOA, MOU, MSA, BPA, SOW, NDA), vendor monitoring. Compliance: reporting, monitoring, consequences, privacy (legal, regulatory, data subject, right to be forgotten). Audits and assessments: internal/external, attestation, penetration testing (physical, offensive/defensive, reconnaissance). Security awareness: phishing campaigns, anomalous behavior recognition, user guidance, training, reporting and monitoring.

extra_guidance: CompTIA Security+ is one of the highest-traffic entry-level cybersecurity certifications - a top volume play. The five domain names and weights above are CompTIA's official SY0-701 objectives - use them verbatim. Emphasis matters: Security Operations is the single heaviest domain at 28% and Threats/Vulnerabilities/Mitigations at 22% - give those the most chapter time. CRITICAL exam-format note: SY0-701 includes performance-based questions (PBQs) that appear FIRST and are interactive simulations (e.g., configure a firewall ruleset, match attack to mitigation, drag controls into categories) - the course and practice tests must prepare learners for PBQ-style scenario tasks, not just multiple choice, and teach the strategy of flagging/skipping time-consuming PBQs and returning to them. Security+ is vendor-neutral, so keep examples technology-agnostic (do not anchor to AWS/Azure/GCP specifics; use generic concepts). Teach the acronym-heavy content with memory aids and clear compare/contrast (e.g., SAML vs OAuth vs OIDC, IDS vs IPS, symmetric vs asymmetric, qualitative vs quantitative risk, SLA vs MOU vs MSA, MTTR vs MTBF vs RTO vs RPO). Practice tests must be scenario-based with realistic distractors and 'BEST/MOST likely' phrasing, mirroring CompTIA's style. RUNWAY NOTE for the business (not for learners): SY0-701 is current now but CompTIA's SY0-801 previews around October 2026 and will add LLM/AI-security content; 701 retires roughly six months after 801 goes live (into 2027). Plan an SY0-801 refresh of this course when 801 is released - and note 801's AI focus dovetails with the SecAI+ course. Funnel note: reference the SecAI+ (AI security) course as the natural next step. Final chapter must be a full exam simulation with a 90-minute time-management strategy for up to 90 questions including PBQ pacing.
